paper_title: WebGLM Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with   Human Preferences
caption: retriever time analysis.
model_annotation: This stacked bar chart illustrates the time, in seconds, spent on different stages of a retrieval process—Search, Extract, Fetch, and Retrieval—across varying percentile thresholds. The horizontal axis represents categories labeled “Avg.”, “50%”, “75%”, and “90%”, arranged alphabetically. The vertical axis, labeled “sec.”, represents time in seconds, with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 8.0 and tick marks at 2.0-second intervals. Each category has a stacked bar composed of four colored segments. The “Search” stage is represented by a dark blue segment, “Extract” by a medium blue segment, “Fetch” by a light blue segment, and “Retrieval” by a pale blue segment.  For "Avg.", the "Search" segment reaches approximately 2.0 sec, “Extract” reaches 1.6 sec, “Fetch” reaches approximately 0.4 sec, and “Retrieval” reaches approximately 1.8 sec, totaling approximately 5.8 sec. For “50%”, the “Search” segment reaches approximately 2.4 sec, “Extract” reaches 1.2 sec, “Fetch” reaches approximately 0.4 sec, and "Retrieval” reaches approximately 1.6 sec, totaling approximately 5.6 sec. For “75%”, the “Search” segment reaches approximately 4.0 sec, “Extract” reaches 2.0 sec, “Fetch” reaches approximately 0.6 sec, and “Retrieval” reaches approximately 1.8 sec, totaling approximately 8.4 sec.  For “90%”, the “Search” segment reaches approximately 6.0 sec, “Extract” reaches 3.0 sec, “Fetch” reaches approximately 0.8 sec, and "Retrieval” reaches approximately 2.0 sec, totaling approximately 11.8 sec. No bars are visually emphasized.
